docs.title: Fontport for FontLab
docs.text:
Fontport bridges FontLab 9 to FontParts and UFO data. It provides detached glyph conversion, live FontParts objects, explicit document access, affine UFO tools and DesignSpace support. It has no UI. Host use requires Python 3.11 arm64; external Python use requires 3.11 or later.

It uses real fontParts, defcon, fontPens, fontTools and ufoLib2 packages without replacing their namespaces or registering a world on import. Native imports are lazy; TypeRig is not required.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
To install into FontLab 9, open install.vfpy from a checkout in FontLab (double-click it or drop it onto FontLab), then restart FontLab. The file is a short stub that hands the work to fontlab-instamix; if instamix is not installed yet, the stub installs it from PyPI first. Instamix installs the package into FontLab's own site-packages and records the install under the extension id com.fontlab.fontport.

FontLab supplies fontlab, fontgate, fontpr and PythonQt. It needs Python packages built for its own Python 3.11 arm64 runtime. The owner manages editable installs into FontLab; do not run host install/uninstall commands yourself. Canonical editable sources may differ from this worktree.

Fontport base installation needs no App. The optional fontlab extra requires fontlab-fontlabapp>=1.2.0 for native edit guards and the legacy feature forwarder. It does not establish registry availability, native acceptance or a release. fontlab-fontlabapp is not on a package index, so pip install "fontlab-fontport[fontlab]" cannot resolve it: install fontlab-fontlabapp from a checkout first. For development, [tool.uv.sources] resolves it from the sibling ../fontlab-fontlabapp checkout, and uv.lock records that path source. See dependencies for package roles and version policy.

docs.title: Detached glyphs and pens
docs.text:
Inside FontLab, use a native glyph and an owned destination:

The examples require installed fontlab-fly>=1.3.0 and their canonical providers. The source installer copies Scripts but does not install or check Fly. Install Fly and its matching providers separately in the same interpreter before running the Scripts or generated startup recipes. The Fontport library has no mandatory Fly dependency.

from fly.fp.transfer import to_fontparts, to_ufo_glyph, write_glyph

snapshot = to_fontparts(native_glyph)  # real fontshell.RGlyph
snapshot.width = 600
write_glyph(snapshot, owned_target)   # retains the target name
ufo_glyph = to_ufo_glyph(owned_target)

Snapshots contain selected-layer contours, components, anchors, metrics, Unicodes, note and plist lib data. They are detached; write_glyph applies them. Native hints, guides, images and other layers are outside this conversion slice. Writes stage input and refuse unsupported identifiers, anchor colors, unnamed anchors, guidelines/images, multiple shapes and transformed targets. An unexpected native assignment error can leave partial changes.

pens.FontGatePointPen accepts point-pen calls. Use fontTools' SegmentToPointPen for segment pens; pens.draw_points draws to another point pen. Open, cubic, quadratic and all-offcurve quadratic contours have offline tests. UFO identifiers have no native storage route and are refused. See UFO interchange for the whole-font sessions and losses.

docs.title: Live fonts
docs.text:
Use the chosen document's MCP font id, distinct from its native pointer id:

from fly.fp.host import NativeFontBackend
from fly.fp.live import RFont

font = RFont(NativeFontBackend(font_id))
font["A"].width = 600
font.info.apply({"familyName": "My Family", "ascender": 810.5},
                undo_name="Edit font information")
font.refresh()  # after external edits or Undo; reacquire child handles
font.close()    # detaches this borrowed binding

Glyphs are real FontParts RGlyph objects backed by defcon notifications. The detached UFOBackend preserves image filenames, all six transformation values and color through checked edits, staged edit_glyph and backend writes. Image payloads stay in the existing UFO image set. Native image transfer still refuses images. Checked glyph.image.data reads and writes actual PNG bytes on UFOBackend; failed image transactions restore the target glyph and newly inserted resource. Shared image assets stay intact. Within font.edit_glyph, PNG bytes and actual image color/transform stay local until the final glyph commits. Clearing an image discards its pending bytes. Staged glyph/image handles expire on context exit; reacquire handles after exit or failed refresh. Native image storage and font-level resource collections remain separate open requirements. Refresh and invalidate() stale loaded child handles; reacquire them after a rejected edit because rollback can reconstruct the glyph. External same-name replacement needs refresh. capabilities() reports explicit backend limits. Native glyph/layer writes use App's canvas-history guard. In a Glyph window, change only shown glyphs; create new glyphs from the Font window. No-ops add no history. Unicode access uses registered font-owned records to avoid fgGlyph's note-mirror loss; native preservation/history qualification remains pending.

owns_document=True closes and discards that document on close; use it only for owned documents. Existing documents are borrowed by default.

world.FontWorld supplies AllFonts, CurrentFont, OpenFont, NewFont and refresh. Open/new handles are owned. world.register() explicitly connects fontParts.world; unregister() restores callbacks. Registration also supports a context manager. Native selection and automatic event subscriptions remain unavailable. MCP save writes a copy, retains dirty state/source paths, and tracks the explicit destination in the Fontport handle.

docs.title: Font data and current limits
docs.text:
• info validates staged metadata before mutation. It supports descriptive name strings, metrics, versions, UPM and selected structured UFO fields. Panose, OS/2 weight/width and stem snaps use the key master. Changing name records refuses without a persistent native route. Concrete native metrics cannot be unset with None; zero is a value. Strict history/persistence checks are opt-in.
  • font.groups is a BaseGroups mapping with detached tuple values. apply replaces all groups; update retains unmentioned groups. Dependent kerning must remain valid. Native names require printable ASCII; divergent both-sided classes refuse. Legacy font-global kerning groups can disappear from VFJ.
  • font.kerning is BaseKerning with explicit and effective lookup. Zero differs from absence; removing an exception restores fallback. Native integer/zero Undo/Redo and VFJ checkpoints exist. Fractional values refuse because native Redo rounds them; keys also have host name restrictions.
  • Features use VFJ-canonical source: font.features.get_blocks() and set_blocks({"prefix": text, "features": [(tag, code)]}). Arbitrary changing whole-text replacement is unsupported. FeatureEdit stages text for compatible models; it does not provide a compiler or bypass the native block boundary.
  • Detached lib staging supports plist data. Native packageLib accepts changed JSON-compatible leaves, with binary/date writes refused; VFJ can reload nested integers as equal-valued floats. Reassign nested values to persist changes.
  • Native geometry uses copy-on-write history with an extra no-op checkpoint. Hinted outline edits, component replacement and some layer operations remain unsupported. Fractional anchors refuse. Exact one-row Undo is not promised.

See native boundaries, feature source and integration. Prior native receipts qualify their recorded build and fixture only.

docs.title: Feature source and the moved editors
docs.text:
Fontport has no UI (issue 201). FontLab editors now live in fontlabapp.fontui (App’s optional fontport extra); they call Fontport lazily, so install them with pip install "fontlab-fontlabapp[fontport]". fontlab_fontport.ui is a tombstone for one release: old factory and module access raises ImportError naming the corresponding App home. The restored factories are:

Factory Input and purpose font_info_editor(font, parent=None, on_apply=None) Stage font information groups_editor(font, parent=None, on_apply=None) Edit explicit groups kerning_editor(font, parent=None, on_apply=None) Inspect/edit kerning transform_editor(font, name=None, parent=None, on_change=None) Preview a detached affine glyph transform batch_panel(recipe, parent=None, on_finish=None, python=None) Run a recipe callback over source UFOs glyph_sequence(font, parent=None, on_select=None) Preview text or slash-separated glyph names 
# old (removed): from fontlab_fontport.ui import font_info_editor
from fly.ap.fontui import font_info_editor

editor = font_info_editor(font)
editor.widget.show()
# Keep editor alive while the panel is open; call editor.close() when finished.

App owns these editors, their lifetime, model, preview and canvas mechanics. The UI facade loads no PythonQt or editor module. Moved editor interaction still needs native acceptance. Glyph sequence layout uses Unicode lookup and UFO kerning fallback, not shaping.

Batch work runs in a separate installed Python 3.11+ interpreter. Pass python= or set FONTLABAPP_BATCH_PYTHON; Start refuses when neither is set. The child uses -I, ignores PYTHONPATH, and receives only PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, USER, LOGNAME and locale variables. Install Fontport in that child environment. Batch destinations must be outside every resolved input UFO tree, including later inputs, symlink aliases, and case or Unicode spellings that the filesystem identifies as the same input. Distinct filesystem objects remain distinct. Existing targets are never overwritten. A destination folder above the inputs is allowed when the generated UFOs are distinct, absent siblings outside all input trees. See the containment defect. The App transform example connects preview and batch. Affine transforms do not preserve stems or provide arbitrary interpolation. fontlabapp.fontui.feature_blocks owns the active-font helpers. The deprecated fontlab_fontport.feature_blocks lazily forwards read_feature_blocks(package) and write_feature_blocks(package, expected, updated, references=..., undo_name=...). They require the original font to be active. Writes compare the source snapshot and referenced glyphs, restore the master, and return {"changed": 0 or 1}. Unexpected host failures can leave partial changes. The import is host-free. Vanilla moved to fontlab_glyport.ui.session; fontlab_fontport.vanilla no longer exists. Scripts use App through fly; general shared UI belongs in App, Glyphs.app compatibility in Glyport, and FontParts/UFO code in Fontport.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Run from this checkout with uv, network access and reviewed App source beside it. uv needs arm64 Python 3.11 or permission to download it. Set FONTLAB_SCRATCH to a writable external-drive folder first; both packages install externally for isolated batch children.

: "${FONTLAB_SCRATCH:?Set FONTLAB_SCRATCH to a writable external-drive folder}"
mkdir -p "$FONTLAB_SCRATCH/tmp" || exit 1
export TMPDIR="$FONTLAB_SCRATCH/tmp" UV_CACHE_DIR
UV_CACHE_DIR="$(mktemp -d "$TMPDIR/fontport-cache.XXXXXX")" || exit 1
for scm_name in $(env | sed -n 's/^\(SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION[^=]*\)=.*/\1/p'); do unset "$scm_name"; done
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1
export PYTHONPATH=src:../fontlab-fontlabapp/src:../fontlab-fly/src
fontport_check() {
  uv run --no-config --python cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64-none --no-project \
    --with pytest --with pytest-cov --with ruff --with defcon \
    --with "fontParts>=1.1.1,<1.2" --with fontPens --with fontTools --with ufoLib2 \
    --with-editable ../fontlab-fontlabapp --with-editable ../fontlab-python-pens \
    --with-editable . "$@"
}
fontport_check python -B -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q
fontport_check python -B -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q -k 'readme or docs_when_app_floor'
fontport_check ruff check --no-cache src tests
Checks run the offline suite, docs and lint; optional compilation needs ufo2ft. The project launcher uses an outdated lock.

Offline tests are not native proof. Native work needs installed artifacts, owned fixtures, import-origin checks and Apply/Undo/Redo/save/reopen comparisons in a dedicated FontLab session. Restart after each mutating suite; never use borrowed user documents. Pass absolute paths and split work around the fixed five-second host deadline. Do not construct a QApplication or second event loop. The startup launcher is a file for host startup, not input to run_python.

docs.text:

Scripts demos use detached sample data, with host-free build_report() results and optional FontLab report windows through Fly/App. No open font is required.

docs.text:
The browser-component record binds the fly-january 0.2.1 and MaterialX 10.1.8 browser assets to exact upstream notices, package archives and source maps. Product terms above remain unchanged.

The English-only omission manifest binds all 35 unused lunr-languages 1.20.0 helpers, including Wordcut and TinySegmenter. The build rejects theme/search-language, corpus, vendor-set/hash and local HTML-reference drift before removing them. Five Fly assets and seven MaterialX assets match the original wheel bytes. The manifest records wheel and output hashes for both MaterialX stylesheets rescaled by Fly. Historical complete outputs remain recovery evidence; omitted helpers are not represented as currently distributed or relicensed.

The main source map retains 211 preferred sources, including 128 exact NPM source matches; the worker map retains 13 sources, including Lunr 2.3.9. The exact clipboard distribution embeds its dependencies; select, good-listener and delegate retain their upstream README MIT link and Zeno Rocha attribution, without invented standalone licence text or dates. CSS maps retain source names without embedded source bodies.

Font Awesome Free retains Fonticons attribution and CC-BY 4.0 terms. Octicons retains GitHub's MIT notice; Lucide retains ISC and inherited notices. Of 45 observed ordered SVG path tuples, 43 match installed MaterialX icon path tuples exactly, including fontawesome/solid/caret-down.svg used by --md-version-icon. docs.title: FontParts yardstick and RoboFab mapping
docs.text:
Regenerate the complete per-ID ledger with uv run python tools/fontparts-coverage.py --reuse-parity. Omit --reuse-parity to re-run host-free parity. Supply --native-evidence with the round14 directory when outside the workspace; the default searches ancestors.

Host-free parity uses FontParts 1.1.1, which exposes fontParts.test.testEnvironment (singular test), with 1,797 IDs. Real upstream fontshell: 1,796 pass, one upstream skip (TestImage.test_bool_data_len_zero: “Cannot set zero data”). The live-font/UFO-backend run: 1,748 pass, 48 UnsupportedCapability, the same skip, zero unclassified failures. Pytest checks every ID and prevents new capability exclusions without updating the reviewed 48-ID baseline.

These counts are not native passes. The per-ID fixtures column distinguishes real live RFont/UFOBackend objects from upstream's detached fontshell objects. The latter are parity checks, not FontGate fixtures. No package namespace is impersonated. Full raw tracebacks/fixture routes are retained in verification/issue-105/round10/{fontshell,memory}.jsonl.

The native callable is fontlab_fontport.testing.object_generator(cls_name):

The examples require installed fontlab-fly>=1.3.0 and their canonical providers.

from fontParts.test import testEnvironment
from fly.fp.testing import ObjectGenerator, generator_context, object_generator

with generator_context(ObjectGenerator()):
    passed = testEnvironment(object_generator, inApp=True)

Do not run that monolithic invocation through run_python. C4 uses round10.py instead: one upstream ID per RPC, followed by separate per-owner cleanup RPCs. Use --native-attached for the attached upstream column (default: orphan column). Each column is observed independently. The f3d7dc5 run separately counts the exact 72 C4-reviewed orphan/parent IDs as HarnessExclusion with capability testing.nativeAttached.parents in attached mode only. The reviewed ID list is in testing_exclusions.py; no assertion text is classified heuristically. All other assertions/bare NotImplementedError remain unclassified failures. The native driver first exercises ObjectGenerator(native_attached=True) for all 16 families. Every native document is created/owned, tracked before wrapper construction, and closed with close_font(save=False) on the finally path. Guideline/image creation returns explicit capability refusals.

Upstream's ordinary object generator requires orphans with no parent. This adapter currently binds registered documents; detached native wrappers are not implemented. This is an adapter limit, not a claim that FontGate has no detached object API. Native orphan requests refuse as testing.nativeOrphan.<family>; attached fixtures must not be presented as passing those parent assertions. Selection is also explicitly unavailable. Native font tests exercise real registered documents. Native assertions and unexpected errors remain failures with tracebacks; the controller never calls them host defects merely because FontLab was involved. C4 must attach a minimal --test-id reproducer and an upstream fl issue to any confirmed host defect.

C4's f3d7dc5 / FontLab 9.0.9783 native run classifies all 1,797 IDs in both modes: orphan 432 pass / 1,365 named capability / 0 unclassified; attached 1,087 pass / 638 named capability / 72 harness exclusions / 0 unclassified. These are C4 observations, not a host-free lane's native run. Source: workspace verification/issue-106/evidence/issue-105/round14/SUMMARY.md, upstream-out/20261016T043446540472Z-49425680/{receipts.jsonl,result.json} and upstream-attached-out/20261016T043701928259Z-14a1ddd8/{receipts.jsonl,result.json}. There are no separate round14 classification JSON files: the generator consumes the actual per-ID classifications in receipts and reconciles both result counts. It rejects missing/duplicate IDs, unnamed capabilities and unclassified results. Pass/capability/harness are separate outcomes; parent harness exclusions are not product failures or native passes. Row 30.1 closure remains controller-owned. The driver exits nonzero for any unclassified result, mismatch or slow phase. Its trace guard checks Python work; a blocking native call cannot be preempted. Any phase reaching four seconds needs a C4 ticket and further splitting.

No FL5 indexes or compatibility aliases are invented. Hint conversion/writes remain outside the supported FontParts surface. Point/segment/contour/glyph selection Selection tests in the full ledger Native/world selection remains a named capability refusal; world registration/open/new/close and all 19 examples pass. File dialogs Outside Fontport (Vanilla session moved to Glyport, fontlab_glyport.ui.session) The f3d7dc5 upstream/world suites do not prove interactive dialogs. Fontport holds no dialog code; Glyport owns that verification.

docs.title: Fontport integration examples and limits
docs.text: These additions have host-free tests. The native handoff is NATIVE-MANIFEST.json, with an owned GetGo probe. Run the host-side CLI through fl-native.sh --mutating. It creates a unique ignored .local/native-issue105/ run directory, warms imports separately, and uses one native operation per call with a four-second timing budget. No native receipt is claimed for these additions.

docs.title: Explicit FontParts environment
docs.text:
The examples require installed fontlab-fly>=1.3.0 and their canonical providers.

from fly.fp.world import FontWorld, register

environment = FontWorld()                 # native imports happen on calls
borrowed = environment.CurrentFont()      # None when no documents exist
with register(environment):
    from fontParts import world
    assert world.CurrentFont() is borrowed
    fonts = world.AllFonts()
# The previous dispatcher is restored, including on an exception.

environment.OpenFont(absolute_owned_copy) and NewFont(...) return owned handles. Their close() discards the owned native document; borrowed close only invalidates that binding. Registration closes no documents. world.RFont() creates a native document while registered; world.RFont(existing_fontport_font) returns the same handle. Native open/new require showInterface=True.

Call environment.refresh() after edits or Undo made outside Fontport. This invalidates loaded layer/glyph snapshots and removes externally closed fonts from the handle cache. Native callbacks are not subscribed automatically, and native CurrentGlyph/selection dispatch raises NotImplementedError explicitly. Native save currently writes a copy; it does not clear FontLab's dirty state or change its source filename. Unexpected native assignment failures are not a transactional rollback facility.

docs.title: Feature editing and font data
docs.text:
from fontParts.fontshell import RFont
from fly.fp.fontdata import FeatureEdit, stage_lib

font = RFont()                            # actual upstream detached environment
edit = FeatureEdit(font.features)
edit.text = "# Ω\nfeature liga { sub f i by fi; } liga;\n"
assert edit.dirty
edit.revert()                            # typing has not changed the font
edit.text = "# Ω\n"
edit.apply()                             # explicit public FontParts text setter
font.lib.update(stage_lib({"nested": {"bytes": b"\x00", "values": [1, True]}}))

Fontport's live features and lib are real BaseFeatures/BaseLib objects. The feature wrapper preserves exact text and distinguishes None from ""; FeatureEdit also works with actual upstream fontshell objects. Feature text is data, never Python, and no compile action is exposed. Native FontGate has separate stored prefix/tag blocks, read through the VFJ-canonical fontpr serializer. Use font.features.get_blocks() and set_blocks({"prefix": text, "features": [(tag, code)]}). Only arbitrary replacement-text splitting is unsupported; see the API contract.

Actual FontParts UFO output preserves CRLF bytes on write; current fontTools UFOReader normalizes CRLF to LF on reopen. A regression records that upstream boundary, rather than claiming byte-exact reloaded feature text.

stage_lib accepts supported XML plist strings, integers, finite reals, booleans, arrays, dictionaries, binary data and naive UTC dates with whole-second precision. It validates serialization without parsing the XML back, preserving CR/CRLF. It canonicalizes arrays to lists and rejects lossy date precision, nonfinite values, invalid nested keys and unserializable values before dispatch. Reads are detached: reassign a nested value to persist changes. lib.update validates changed values as a batch; lib.apply replaces the mapping while leaving unchanged foreign leaves opaque, including inside nested mappings and arrays. Foreign JSON null/control text/large integers survive valid sibling edits. Array leaves match by index; moving a foreign leaf counts as a new write.

Native font lib uses flPackage.packageLib and currently permits JSON-compatible values only, for changed leaves, with new numbers within the exact JSON integer range. Unchanged foreign values are deep-copied without plist/JSON normalization. Binary/date data is refused before native history/mutation. This application-level map is not proof of automatic fgFont.lib or native UFO-export synchronization.

info.apply additionally stages descriptive name/legal fields, localized openTypeNameRecords, OS/2 weight/width/Panose and PostScript horizontal/vertical stem lists. It uses fontTools' UFO3 validators plus native numeric bounds, with detached structured values. These native routes need individual persistence and Undo proof. The advertised native postscriptBlueValues setter is unimplemented and remains unavailable. Optional metric clearing remains unavailable too.

docs.title: Vanilla controls moved to Glyport
docs.text:
Fontport holds only FontParts and UFO code. It has no Vanilla session and no UI shim for windows, controls or dialogs. VanillaSession moved to fontlab_glyport.ui.session (issue 122). Install the separately distributed fontlab-glyport wheel for it; Fontport does not depend on Glyport.

# old (removed): from fontlab_fontport.vanilla import VanillaSession
from fly.gp.ui.session import VanillaSession

fontlab_fontport.vanilla has been deleted (issue 201; its one-release tombstone expired). Session behaviour, window ownership and teardown are documented with Glyport. The FontParts-bound editors (font info, groups, kerning, transform, batch, glyph sequence) now live in fontlabapp.fontui; install App’s fontport extra. The old fontlab_fontport.ui package only raises migration errors and goes in the next release. Active-font feature I/O also lives in fontlabapp.fontui.feature_blocks; the deprecated Fontport path forwards lazily and needs Fontport’s optional fontlab extra.

docs.title: Detached B09 operations
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from ufoLib2 import Font
from fly.fp.operations import BatchRunner, Recipe, transform_font
from fly.fp.designspace import Designspace

root = Path("/absolute/owned-output")
recipe = Recipe(matrix=(1.2, 0, 0, 1, 10, 0), intensity=50)
with Font.open(root / "owned-source.ufo") as source:
    preview = transform_font(source, recipe)
preview.save(root / "new-output.ufo", overwrite=False)
recipe.save("new-settings.json")            # exclusive creation
assert Recipe.load("new-settings.json") == recipe
inspectable_python = recipe.script()         # returned text; never auto-executed
for result in BatchRunner().run([(root / "owned-source.ufo", root / "batch-output.ufo")], recipe):
    print(result.ok, result.error)
model = Designspace.open("owned.designspace")
coordinates = model.defaults()
instance = model.instance(coordinates)       # always labelled as an instance

These are affine transforms with explicit enable/intensity/reset semantics, using fontTools pens. They transform outlines/anchors/guides/images/components without modifying source objects. Whole-font component transforms are conjugated to avoid scaling transformed bases twice. Width/height are scalar advance-vector projections; font metrics and kerning are retained. No stem/topology-preserving or interpolation method is simulated. Singular matrices are refused.

Designspace reads actual source/instance locations from fontTools descriptors, maps design to user coordinates, reports missing source files and validates axis endpoints/defaults. Designspace.from_native(backend) snapshots native axes/master/instance locations without switching the current source. Echopy sidecars and native flAxis bindings confirm its native map is design→user; the adapter reverses it for fontTools. GetGo comparison is still required. Discrete axes, anisotropic locations and multi-axis maps are explicitly unavailable.

BatchRunner eagerly preflights and reserves at call time (before returning an iterator), accepts at most 256 UFO source/destination pairs, and forbids overwrite/case-insensitive duplicate targets, yields per-attempt results, resets running state on failure/cancel/iterator close and can call progress/cancellation callbacks. Exhaust or close its iterator; close works before the first next call too. A large single-file transform is synchronous and belongs outside FontLab's UI thread. The native acceptance driver processes a small owned UFO inside FontLab, one attempt per RPC with progress/native document polls between calls and a <4 s budget. That tests cooperative between-file responsiveness for this fixture; large-font preemption and UI scheduling remain Fontlabapp acceptance work. Partial output may remain after a write failure; a batch is not an atomic transaction. export_ufo_subset/compile_ttf remain selected geometry export/external compilation, not complete native font conversion.

Fontport needs no Glyport. The manifest command may still add import roots via --extra-source. Append --dry-run to the Python driver invocation to check source origins without connecting or copying fixtures (do not invoke the mutating wrapper for a host-free dry run). Fontport package trees are purged in FontLab and imported __file__ paths asserted against preflight results. Native phases let the normal event loop process deferred deletion between RPCs. After every mutating run, including failure, restart the test FontLab before the next suite. The shared fl-native.sh manages sessions but does not perform this post-run restart.

docs.title: API sources
docs.text:
Implementation uses the official FontParts environment contracts, fontTools transform pens, designspace descriptors, UFO validators and ufoLib2 copying/reference APIs, plus the installed upstream source and native binding declarations. Runtime proof and source inspection are recorded separately in the manifest/work log.

Host-facing open, save, subset export, compilation and batch APIs refuse relative paths instead of consulting FontLab's process cwd.

docs.title: Pens on live FontParts objects
docs.text:
Use real upstream classes; Fontport never registers substitute namespaces. Caller owns the destination font and precreates output glyphs in a separate phase. font.edit_glyph stages an operation on an ordinary detached fontshell glyph, commits once and invalidates loaded handles. Fetch a fresh glyph after commit. Exceptions inside the context write nothing.

The examples require installed fontlab-fly>=1.3.0 and their canonical providers.

from fly.fp.recipes import digest, bounds, flatten, transform_into

live_digest = digest(font['A'])   # actual fontPens.DigestPointPen
rectangle = bounds(font['A'], font)  # actual fontTools.BoundsPen
flatten(font, 'A', 'fontport_flat')  # actual fontPens.FlattenPen
transform_into(font, 'A', 'fontport_shifted', (1, 0, 0, 1, 25, 0))

Flatten decomposes components through the live glyph set, then writes the whole path once. Native Undo-row behavior remains a C4 gate; one backend commit alone does not prove one native Undo row. Fractional anchor/hint/shared-shape limits still apply to live destinations. Use an owned empty destination, not a hinted GetGo source glyph.

MarginPen and TransformPointPen use the same real RGlyph interfaces:

from fontPens.marginPen import MarginPen
from fontPens.transformPointPen import TransformPointPen

pen = MarginPen(font, 200, isHorizontal=False)
font['A'].draw(pen)
margins_at_200 = pen.getMargins()
with font.edit_glyph('fontport_shifted', undo_name='Shifted point-pen path') as target:
    target.clearContours()
    font['A'].drawPoints(TransformPointPen(target.getPointPen(), (1, 0, 0, 1, 25, 0)))

Designspace.from_native(font._backend) snapshots native axis/user maps, master design locations and instances using fontTools.designspaceLib. It does not create interpolated native instances. Native map keys are design coordinates; the adapter reverses them to fontTools' (user, design) pairs.

parse_features(font.features.text, font.keys(), classes=dict(font.groups)) uses feaLib with native OT classes supplied separately; features.text excludes panel classes intentionally. Includes are not followed automatically. Parse errors retain locations and need comparison with fonts FontLab actually compiles; syntax acceptance is not a native compile action.

C4 --suite pens warms imports, then reads/tests one native glyph at a time, records raw digests and native/bounds rectangles, snapshots axes/masters and parses features. Flatten edit, Undo and Redo are separate calls with full expected/observed payload receipts. Repeat against static and variable GetGo copies and return any slow phase or mismatch as a ticket.

Round-12 correction: bounds() keeps the actual curve extrema from BoundsPen. FontLab's native boundingBox includes off-curve controls. Use control_bounds(glyph, font) (ControlBoundsPen) for the native comparison; the native receipt keeps both boxes. No y-axis inversion is inferred or hidden.

A live native contour may be built one point at a time. Empty contours allocate no native geometry; incomplete controls or other temporarily invalid point sequences stay in the Python model until a valid path exists. Native data is unchanged during that interval. Saving an unfinished path raises glyph.incompleteContours; finish/correct/remove it first. Standalone pens still reject malformed paths. Identifiers refuse as identifiers before native writes. The attached upstream generator supplies an empty contour, matching the upstream factory, rather than inserting a triangle into every contour fixture.

Round-13 flattening puts fontTools RoundingPen between FlattenPen and the destination pen. Each sampled coordinate rounds to the nearest integer using fontTools otRound (half-way ties towards positive infinity). The rounding error is at most 0.5 units per axis per sample; FlattenPen's curve approximation error is separate. The native driver builds its expected digest through the same rounding pen before comparing readback, Undo and Redo.

Round-14 history correction: a staged commit uses copy-on-write native shapes after the baseline notification. The native pre/post protocol has an extra no-op row, exposed as glyph.exactSingleUndo=False. The first Undo must restore actual MCP contour/point records. One backend commit does not mean one visible Undo row.

docs.title: Native boundaries for B05/B06 and live handles
docs.text:
The App can import NATIVE_CAPABILITIES and STRUCTURED_ROUTES from fontlab_fontport.capabilities, or ask NativeFontBackend.capabilities() for a detached snapshot. A false capability is an explicit contract, not a probe that mutates a document. glyph.externalChangeNotifications is false: native edits/Undo/Redo do not notify defcon automatically. Show “Reload required”, call font.refresh() and reacquire glyph/layer handles. Adapter-originated accepted edits still mark defcon dirty and invalidate component representations.

StaleObjectError identifies closed documents and invalidated/removed bindings. Public cached glyph/child/info/group/kerning/feature/lib reads check the owner; backend IDs are reacquired rather than retaining FontLab native pointers. A private .naked() defcon object deliberately obtained before closure is outside the guarded FontParts API. Do not keep/use native wrappers after closure.

Boundary Current contract / C4 reproducer Exact one info Undo row D18 default require_single_undo=False keeps info editable with the verified extra no-op row. Opt-in True refuses changing batches before checkpoint/write. C4 single-undo phases test the refusal; structured phases explicitly opt into legacy history to probe real setters Optional absent metric None raises UnsupportedCapability('info.<field>.absent', ...), before any assignment/checkpoint; no zero is written. Concrete native master doubles do not encode absence. C4 unset-metric phases Unicode native classes Changing mappings containing Unicode class names raise groups.unicodeNames before native construction/write/history. Existing identical mappings remain no-ops. C4 unicode-class phases Divergent both-sided classes One native class has one membership array. Divergent public.kern1/kern2 projections of that same native group raise groups.divergentBothSides during planning, before writes/checkpoints. C4 both-sided phases require a real KernBothSide fixture; a missing prerequisite is a failed native acceptance check Legacy native group flags / VFJ require_persistence=True is opt-in; the default False preserves v1.0.0 editing/save. Font-global groups not in FeaClassGroupMode cause changing group mappings and VFJ saves to refuse before writes/history. Ordinary feature/current-master groups remain editable. Explicit False opts into the old route. C4 creates an owned legacy-mode fixture, verifies group-write/save refusal and file absence, then removes it before structured setter checks. Original FontLab flag loss still needs an upstream issue Fractional native kerning Any changing operation involving current/requested fractional kerning raises kerning.fractionalHistory before writes/history. An identical fractional snapshot remains a no-op. C4 fractional-kerning phases Fractional native anchors _stage_source refuses as glyph.anchor.precision before import/native staging or target writes. A rejected live edit restores the accepted defcon model. C4 glyph/fractional-anchor phases Non-ASCII glyph names glyph.name.unicodeVfj refuses before native create/rename/geometry writes. No speculative encoding conversion. C4 glyph/unicode-name phases

D18 preserves the v1.0.0 default editing contract. Info edits and saves work; strict history/persistence checks are opt-in (require_single_undo=True on info.apply, require_persistence=True on backend group/save operations). Untouched legacy groups and Unicode glyph names do not block ordinary saves. Fontport refuses unsafe new glyph names, fractional anchors/kerning and other unroundtrippable edits before writing; these never become save-time surprises. It does not certify that FontLab preserves every foreign baseline field. The extra-checkpoint and legacy-VFJ defects remain unresolved host behavior. C4 owns filing/linking the fl issues with the actual build, original failing receipts and minimal reproducer.

docs.title: Structured storage correction after C4 T9
docs.text:
The fg::Style setters are not evidence of native persistence. C4 on 9.0.9783 measured lost Panose/weight/width/name-record writes after Undo/VFJ reopening. The master-backed routes now used by Fontport match Font Info:

Field Bound property / source Persisted storage / source openTypeOS2Panose flPackage.panose string; Proteus/pygate/pyflpackage.cpp:1512–1516 keyPackageMaster._panose, flpackage.cpp:17199–17220; master writer :5875 openTypeOS2WeightClass flPackage.weight_value; pyflpackage.cpp:949 keyPackageMaster._weight_value, flpackage.cpp:17350–17354; writer :5853 openTypeOS2WidthClass flPackage.width_value; pyflpackage.cpp:951 keyPackageMaster._width_value, flpackage.cpp:17356–17360; writer :5854 openTypeNameRecords Changing writes refuse info.openTypeNameRecords.persistence info setter mutates regenerated fg::Style names (pyflpackage.cpp:2031–2078). Font Info writes localizedNames via setLocalizedNames (workspace2/fontinfo_data.cpp:520; flpackage.cpp:16806–16836), absent from the Python bindings/stubs. MCP set_font_info's global whitelist (common/mcp/mcptools_fonts.cpp:469–565) has no localized/name-record route. postscriptStemSnapH/V Existing info setters, pyflpackage.cpp:3197,3237 Existing native stem routes; C4 T9 did not report their Undo/VFJ failure

The model source paths above are under Proteus/common/model/. Font Info itself loads master values at fontinfo_data.cpp:391–392 and Panose at :402, then stores the same properties at :586–596. Panose's empty native string reads as absent (None), not invented zeros. Weight/width getter rounding follows fg::round.

All validation and name-record refusal precede checkpoints or writes, including mixed batches. Master-backed writes retain package/mastersContainer pre/post notifications. C4 must re-run the phased read/edit/Undo/Redo/VFJ checks; source verification and mocked checkpoints do not prove the new route natively. The catalogue marks the derived name-record getter as bound but write=None, write_supported=False, rather than advertising the nonpersistent setter.

docs.title: Named native limits and lib keys
docs.text:
Dangling native kerning glyph/group references refuse kerning.danglingNames; MCP's own group creation resolves actual flGlyph objects before its command (common/mcp/mcptools_metrics_kerning.cpp:709–715). Plain feature classes retain their existing mapping policy. No phantom glyphs are created. Unresolved/cyclic components refuse components.unresolvedBase, identifiers refuse identifiers, and unsetting concrete non-metric info refuses info.unset. Metric absence retains the more specific info..absent name.

Native QVariant tuples are recursively exposed as UFO lists. The known host key com.fontlab.kerningClassesInMainMaster is hidden from public font.lib keys, kept unchanged through edits/clear, and cannot be assigned through that view (lib.reservedKey). Other foreign lib entries remain visible and keep the existing unchanged-leaf preservation contract.

docs.title: Master scope and unfinished geometry (Round 13)
docs.text:
Panose, OS/2 weight and OS/2 width writes affect the key master only, not every master. Their package properties delegate to keyPackageMaster (source locations in the table above); batch callers must not infer all-master edits.

Invalidation, refresh, save and staged edits refuse glyph.incompleteContours while provisional point sequences remain. Closing emits a RuntimeWarning with that capability name before discarding provisional edits and closing the owned document with save=False. This permits fixture cleanup without silently losing editing state. Complete or remove provisional contours before invalidating.

Non-integral UPM refuses info.unitsPerEm.fractional before writes. Integral floats and integer subclasses used by UFO OS/2 weight/width exports are accepted; bools are not numeric metrics.

docs.title: Round-14 history and explicit master scope
docs.text:
glyph.exactSingleUndo is false: pre/post notifications add a no-op checkpoint in addition to the restoring edit. Working shapes are cloned after the baseline notification to keep stored geometry untouched. The first Undo must restore contours.

capabilities() exposes each Panose/weight/width/stem-snap route with bound: "key-master"; STRUCTURED_ROUTES reports the same scope. No per-master write argument is advertised. Invalid per-side native class membership refuses groups.multiMembership before mutation/history.

Round-15 read comparisons exclude only root MCP lastModified, named fontlab.lastModified: it is an edit/save timestamp, not a reversible font value. Raw receipts retain it; nested lib values with that name remain significant. Glyph creation history is counted on the package, subsequent glyph edits on the glyph graph. Undo/Redo/reopen payload and geometry comparisons remain gates.

docs.title: Native feature storage (FontLab 9)
docs.text:
Fontport reads VFJ-canonical feature text and writes explicit ordered blocks. The Round-4 claim that no lossless native route existed was wrong: it missed fontpr.get_font_info, which uses the VFJ writer, and the equivalence of the bound fragment setters to FontLab's VFJ loader. This document supersedes that claim. Native timing, first Undo/Redo and saved-artifact proof remain required.

blocks = font.features.get_blocks()
# {"prefix": "...", "features": [("kern", "feature kern {...} kern;\n"), ...]}
tag, code = blocks["features"][0]
blocks["features"][0] = (tag, code + "\n# edited code\n")
font.features.set_blocks(blocks, undo_name="Edit feature")
assert font.features.text == blocks["prefix"] + "".join(code for tag, code in blocks["features"])

NativeFontBackend exposes the same operations as get_feature_blocks() and set_feature_blocks(). Reads are detached. Prefix and feature strings preserve Unicode, CR/CRLF, whitespace and comments; feature order is explicit. OT panel classes remain separate font groups and are not duplicated into the prefix.

docs.title: Exact read path
docs.text:
fontpr.get_font_info(font_id=...) returns the openTypeFeatures array, with an optional first {feature: prefix} entry followed by ordered {name, feature} entries. blocks_from_info(info) parses that snapshot; features.text joins its prefix and feature strings. Missing openTypeFeatures means empty stored text, including a binary-only font. Malformed/unrecognized records raise rather than being silently dropped.

VFJ permits named empty records such as {"name": "ccmp"}: its loader defaults an omitted feature to an empty QString and stores an empty named slot. The text-block API omits these textless slots (including explicit empty strings), and ignores entirely empty anonymous records just as the loader does. Raw read_info snapshots and driver receipts retain every original array record. Sixteen GetGo VFJs have these empty named slots. A no-op text write preserves them; a changing write refuses that current baseline before mutation, naming the empty tag: the whole-text Undo stream cannot reconstruct a tag with no text. This is an explicit native history limitation, not an unknown-record error.

Do not use fgOTLayout.get_prefix() as this source: it requests synthesized panel classes. Do not use keys()/get_feature() either: they can fall back to binary decompilation when stored FEA text is absent. Fontport has no such fallback. If embedded fontpr is unavailable, reading fails explicitly with RuntimeError.

docs.title: Exact structured write path
docs.text:
The entire {prefix: str, features: [(tag, code), ...]} batch is validated before history or mutation. Tags require four printable ASCII bytes, unique names and aalt first if present (native storage forces it to the front). Strings must be UTF-8 encodable and NUL-free. Syntax is stored without compilation.

Changing native writes refuse prefixes that require language-system synthesis. The native test is a literal languagesystem substring (even in a comment), or an initial nonblank/noncomment line starting with include. Its scan splits on LF or lone CR, trimming only space/tab/LF: a CRLF blank line retains \r and stops the scan, so an include after it does not suppress synthesis. LF blank lines are skipped. Otherwise FontLab can prepend a #> languagesystem block during metadata reads or save/reopen. Its generated script/language pairs depend on font glyph Unicode values, feature bodies and native build options; the pure structured API lacks that context and does not guess. stage_blocks checks only split-back fidelity. write_blocks stages first, reads the current snapshot, and returns immediately for identical values. Only a changing staged value receives the synthesis check, before history/mutation; the current Undo baseline never does. Feature-less fonts with no feaTextStorage have no serializer injection, so their identical empty writes succeed and an explicit language-system feature add is allowed. Changing/clearing a nonempty font to an empty prefix still raises a precise ValueError, because clear/set_prefix would allocate storage that can synthesize text. Reads remain available for every snapshot.

Undo/Redo restores a concatenated FEA stream through FontLab's whole-text splitter, not through the VFJ array loader. Consequently stage_blocks and set_blocks simulate that splitter with the pure split_history_text function in native_feature_split.py. The acceptance rule is exact: concatenate the prefix and ordered codes, simulate history loading, and require exactly the same prefix and (tag, code) pairs back. There is no raw-keyword prohibition.

The simulation works on UTF-8 byte offsets with the native destructive strtok semantics and delimiter set. When the next non-delimiter character is #, the entire comment line is one token; feature inside it never splits a block. After a header the native algorithm seeks the first matching tag token before looking for the next feature token. Thus normal aalt references such as feature sups; before the closing tag are accepted. Like native code, this is not a brace-aware grammar: a matching tag token earlier in a body can affect where the next keyword search begins. The simulation also models duplicate-tag retention, aalt placement, LF appending by FeaTextBlock and name-table extraction.

Leading comments/whitespace in a named code, a different declared tag, multiple independent blocks in one pair, or a name table removed on history loading are refused when they change the reconstructed model. ValueError identifies the affected prefix/block and differing prefix, tag, code or block count before history or mutation. A changing write checks the current Undo baseline too. A tagless trailing feature is refused before native calls: the native loader can read past its heap buffer at token + 8 (reviewer's ASan probe). The Round-6 blanket rejection of comment/body keywords was wrong and is replaced by this simulation. Reads preserve nonempty native fragments without imposing write-side split-back checks. Actual native array/whole-text/class receipts remain required; the simulation neither compiles nor validates general FEA.

Writes replay the VFJ loader: fgFont.features.clear(), set_prefix(prefix), then set_feature(tag, code) in order. clearFeaText(false) leaves group classes untouched. The backend initializes package history and wraps writes with notifyChangesApplied(name, [package, package.featuresContainer()]) before/after, calling notifyFeaturesChanged(font_id, False) after the fragment writes. Identical writes and invalid batches add no history. Unexpected native failures can leave partial writes; this is not an atomic transaction.

features.text = existing_text is a no-op. Native None is a no-op when already feature-less; clearing existing features is refused by the synthesis guard above. A different arbitrary text string raises UnsupportedCapability with capability font.features.text.split: only native whole-text splitting (setFeaText/loadFeaTextInfo) remains unbound. The pure simulation validates explicit text blocks; it does not enable arbitrary FEA import through the text setter. Use the structured setter for history-stable blocks, subject to the empty-slot baseline limitation above.

docs.title: Canonicalization and source evidence
docs.text:
Paths below refer to the read-only native source tree and captured declarations.

Contract Primary evidence Embedded callable APIs Echopy fontpr.pyi:27,87, fontgate.pyi:3573–3618, fontlab.pyi:6767,9901. Proteus/common/mcp/fontpr_module.cpp:139–145,196–212 registers tools and directly calls MCPTools::callTool, without loopback HTTP. mcptools.cpp:713 explicitly permits fontpr calls inside run_python; only recursive run_python/output calls are blocked. Canonical serializer mcptools_fonts.cpp:796–811 calls packageInfoJson; Proteus/common/model/flpackage.cpp:6089–6118 calls the same writeFeatures used for VFJ save. JSON writer flblockwriterqjson.cpp:53–55 always uses formatJSON; bin_types.cpp:642,644 names the fields. Prefix without panel classes, feature order flpackage.cpp:6925–6965: dumpFeaPrefix(..., false) plus ordered feature dumps, guarded by hasFeaText. VFJ-equivalent writes flpackage.cpp:10215–10252: clearFeaText(false), setPrefixText and ordered setFeatureText. pyfontgate/fgotlayout.cxx:280–312 binds those same calls. Default false is in FontGate/opentype/layout.h:817; l_fea.cpp:3212–3238 forces aalt first. Whole-text equivalence FontGate/opentype/layout.cpp:1277–1284 and l_fea.cpp:3574–3612: dumpFeaText(false) uses the same prefix output plus feature texts. Language synthesis layout.cpp:1387–1390 defines hasFeaText by storage existence; flpackage.cpp:6931 returns before serialization when storage is absent. A no-op does not allocate storage. l_fea.cpp:3299–3357 checks the literal marker/initial include exception; xml/xml_write_aux.cpp:63–75 trims only space/tab/LF. dumpPrefixText at 4384–4398 emits the auto-tagged block; flpackage.cpp:6938–6942 calls it for VFJ/metadata. Pairs depend on glyph scripts/build configuration (l_fea.cpp:472–546) and feature languages (549–590,3015–3034). Only changing staged values receive the prefix refusal; current Undo baselines do not. Table-name correction l_fea.cpp:3362–3432 extracts a name table on whole-text loading; its tablesTexts output is commented out in dumpFeaFile at 3585–3602. A structured prefix could otherwise store table code verbatim, but the split-back check now refuses it because Undo would extract it. Empty named records flpackage.cpp:10224–10252 defaults feature/name to empty QString, ignores an entirely empty record, and stores a named empty slot with setFeatureText. l_fea.cpp:2877–2884,3120–3130,4452–4461 keeps the tag while dumping no code. The text API omits textless slots; changing native writes refuse this unrepresentable history baseline. History flpackage.cpp:2399–2455 featuresContainer serializes/restores feature state. writeFeaturesFea at 6978–6990 dumps whole text; readFeaturesFea/readFeatures at 7523–7563,7610 restore via setFeaText. l_fea.cpp:3037–3070,3435–3560 tokenizes/splits and re-keys blocks; layout.cpp:741–749 appends LF to nonempty fragments. Exact simulated split-back equality replaces the Round-6 keyword guard.

The read-only corpus regression covers 99/99 GetGo VFJs: all stage unchanged and all identical writes succeed before native allocation/history. There are 85 with feature records and 14 feature-less fonts. Only changing writes that add features without a language-system prefix are refused for those 14. Corpus discovery prefers an existing FONTPORT_GETGO_DIR, then searches every ancestor of the test file for fontlab-python-examples/testdata/getgo; it skips only when none exists. Both canonical/worktree layouts are tested. A temporary standalone C++ probe compiles the inspected tokenizer/loader functions with minimal storage stubs; the Python history simulation matches their outputs for all 99 fonts and 12 edge cases, including a single-line name table whose unread last byte survives rdbuf. This is source-level host-free evidence, not FontLab runtime/Undo proof. The old probe and its per-font hash receipts were removed with the round tooling (issue 201); they remain in git history.

docs.title: Five-second deadline and native acceptance
docs.text:
get_font_info includes groups, masters, info, hinting, tables and lib, but no outline traversal. Its native schema supports only detail=full or hinting; there is no narrower feature-only filter in the inspected binding. Repeating or chunking Python work cannot interrupt one metadata serialization call.

The driver warms imports separately, then performs one read/write/history/save/ reopen operation per call, enforcing <4 s wall time. --features-only isolates B08 and adds a separate Plum variable-font metadata timing call after Medio. If either call exceeds budget, split handoff at the RPC boundary: obtain a get_font_info snapshot as a direct external MCP tool call outside run_python, then use blocks_from_info for detached parsing. This moves the read outside the fixed run_python deadline; it does not prove a faster native serializer or make an oversized write safe. The synchronous backend write still reads current metadata for its no-op check. No deadline-safe large-font claim is made yet.

The native driver edits one Medio feature, checks byte-equal UTF-8 strings and order with classes unchanged, tests first Undo/Redo, saves/reopens the edit, then restores the original blocks and saves/reopens again to compare original bytes. Receipts return rows_equal, whole_text_equal and classes_equal independently, along with observed arrays, classes, joined text and observed/expected SHA-256 hashes. A mismatch does not raise before returning evidence: the runner retains the receipt, marks acceptance failed and continues the remaining phases and cleanup. A row-boundary/tag difference can thus be distinguished from text loss. No-op and arbitrary-split refusal phases also record flags, observed history states and exception type/message/capability instead of asserting. Missing named fixture features and unavailable staged edits likewise become acceptance flags. The separate feature-synthesis-refusal phase attempts an empty-prefix edit, records the precise refusal and unchanged history, and retains a failing receipt if the refusal or history check differs. Native execution uses the shared mutating-session runner and owned GetGo copies, then requires a FontLab restart. Host-free replay tests are not native receipts.

docs.title: Round 10 handoff to C4
docs.text:
Current corrections and re-run observations: Round 12.

This implementation was developed without FontLab or Remopy. Native timings, payloads, exact Undo rows and VFJ persistence are not verified here. Keep issues/105 rows 27/30/31 open until C4 has the receipts required by GAPS.md.

From this worktree, C4 runs each command separately in a fresh dedicated session:

sh tests/native_drivers/run-round10.sh --suite upstream
sh tests/native_drivers/run-round10.sh --suite glyph
sh tests/native_drivers/run-round10.sh --suite world
sh tests/native_drivers/run-round10.sh --suite interchange
sh tests/native_drivers/run-round10.sh --suite pens
sh tests/native_drivers/run-round10.sh --suite boundaries
sh tests/native_drivers/run-round10.sh --suite lifecycle

The wrapper uses verification/issue-104/fl-native.sh --mutating --lane C4. It resolves this checkout and workspace, then runs the controller with the checkout project environment, with the local Remopy project added for native execution. Offline --dry-run uses the same checkout plus Remopy dependency environment and bypasses the host wrapper. Restart FontLab after each mutating command, including failures. The controller requires no open documents, purges stale Fontport/driver modules before warming, puts its own src first and checks __file__. Output goes to unique ignored .local/round10/<UTC>-<uuid>/. It copies the corpus before opening, hashes the original, tracks only owned IDs, and closes those IDs with close_font(save=False) in finally. No user documents, Qt application, timers, or deferred-delete flushes are used.

For variable and non-Latin checks repeat the commands with an absolute --fixture /.../getgo/.../font.vfj. Use cc0/plum/plum-var.vfj for variable axes, cc0/medi/medi.vfj for Latin and apache/zotosans/zotosans-georgian.vfj for non-Latin interchange (one master, 127 source glyphs, two feature rows). The latter does not need A/V; the example/pens/geometry suites do. All suites default to Medio. Artifacts: repeat --source /absolute/installed/site-packages (for independent wheel and sdist installs); checkout src must be excluded for those runs. --source is repeatable for actual dependency roots.

Exact extra fixture commands, still one command per restarted native session:

FONTPORT_WORKSPACE="$PWD"
while [ ! -f "$FONTPORT_WORKSPACE/verification/issue-104/fl-native.sh" ]; do
    [ "$FONTPORT_WORKSPACE" != / ] || exit 2
    FONTPORT_WORKSPACE=$(dirname "$FONTPORT_WORKSPACE")
done
FONTPORT_GETGO="$FONTPORT_WORKSPACE/fontlab-python-examples/testdata/getgo"
sh tests/native_drivers/run-round10.sh --suite glyph --fixture "$FONTPORT_GETGO/cc0/plum/plum-var.vfj"
sh tests/native_drivers/run-round10.sh --suite pens --fixture "$FONTPORT_GETGO/cc0/plum/plum-var.vfj"
sh tests/native_drivers/run-round10.sh --suite interchange --fixture "$FONTPORT_GETGO/cc0/plum/plum-var.vfj"
sh tests/native_drivers/run-round10.sh --suite interchange --fixture "$FONTPORT_GETGO/apache/zotosans/zotosans-georgian.vfj"

Offline controller checks (safe in this host-free lane):

uv run python tests/native_drivers/round10.py --suite upstream --list-tests
uv run python tests/native_drivers/round10.py --suite glyph --dry-run
sh -n tests/native_drivers/run-round10.sh

Each phase has a three-second Python trace guard and a measured four-second RPC gate. The upstream suite additionally checks a 2.5-second Python budget. Warm imports, open, edit, snapshots, Undo, Redo, save, close and reopen are separate calls. Export/import advance one glyph or metadata unit per call; bulk UFO disk serialization runs in the client. Native C++ calls cannot be interrupted by a Python trace guard. A slow C++ call is a failed timing gate, never evidence that an arbitrary call is preemptible. C4 must return its phase/timing as a ticket. The controller polls the host between feature phases. It schedules no background work that could outlive its lock.

receipts.jsonl keeps every result, expected/observed payload, equality flag, exception and timing. Each upstream ID has one result line plus separate cleanup lines. A mismatch or unknown failure causes exit 1 and remains in result.json. Known named capability refusals are records, not aborts. No assertion prevents an observation being written. Unknown native failures require C4 classification and an fl issue; no issue number or native pass is fabricated by this lane.

Brief item Code and phases Acceptance / remaining limit 1 / 30.1 testing.py; upstream_steps.py; --suite upstream; FONTPARTS-COVERAGE.md 1,797 IDs; explicit native orphan contract; attached native fixtures attempted separately. Guideline/image fixtures refuse. Native classification pending 2 / 30.2 FONTPARTS-COVERAGE.md introduction + per-ID ledger Full RoboFab checklist mapping; distinguish a passing deprecated dispatch test from native cache-update proof 3 / 27.1 live.edit_glyph; host.write_glyph_named; round10_glyph_steps.py One backend write/notification for staged geometry; exact native first Undo/row count still needs C4. Unsupported topology/component replacement/guides/hinted/shared writes refuse. Unicode names now refuse before create/write 4 / 27.6 world.register/unregister; deploy.write_launcher; 19 examples; round10_world_steps.py Persistent/context registration restore real callbacks; launcher only writes its explicit path; CurrentGlyph/selection named refusal. New/Open/current/all callbacks and all scripts get native receipts 5 / 27.4 interchange.py; round10_interchange_steps.py Full supported UFO model round-trip host-free; incremental native export, strict single-layer native import, compare and VFJ reopen. Loss inventory in UFO-INTERCHANGE.md. Multilayer native import refuses before allocation 6 / 27.2–3 recipes.py; round10_pen_steps.py Per-glyph digest vs the same export read path, native rectangle vs BoundsPen; flatten Undo/Redo; Designspace native axes/master receipts; feaLib parse with native classes. Native all-GetGo execution pending 7 / 30.3 capabilities.NATIVE_CAPABILITIES glyph.externalChangeNotifications.supported == False; App can show “Reload required”. No automatic dirty/representation coherence is claimed 8 / 30.4 host._stage_source; native_kerning; glyph/fractional-anchor and boundary/fractional-kerning phases Exact named refusals before native writes/history; host-free rollback/preflight tested 9 / 31.6 / 31.1 capabilities.STRUCTURED_ROUTES; round10_boundary_steps.py Master-backed Panose/weight/width routes; changing name-record writes refuse explicitly (Round 12). D18 default info/save remains editable; strict refusals are opt-in. Owned both-sided/legacy fixtures are created in separate setup phases; see NATIVE-BOUNDARIES.md 10 / 27.7 errors.StaleObjectError; lifetime.py; live_objects.py; round10_lifecycle_steps.py Cached glyph/point/lib/info/layer reads check owner lifetime. External owned close + explicit VFJ save/reopen phases. Native proof pending

The native geometry suite retains complete target glyph payloads (including other layers/hints) through first Undo/Redo and reopen. C4 must review the edit-to-baseline diff and count/name the native Undo rows; an RPC notification count is not a native Undo-row proof. Source only confirms the two-string component constructor in Proteus/pygate/pyflshape.cpp:65–79; it is missing from the captured flShape constructor list, so this particular mandatory two-argument overload stays positional. Optional native overload arguments remain keywords.

The Ω guard follows C4's measured Ω → Î© kerning-source2 VFJ result. Inspected flglyph.cpp:2768,3043 writes UTF-8 binary tags, which does not isolate the VFJ bug. We therefore refuse non-ASCII native glyph creation/rename/geometry writes, component references, and saves of documents already containing such names rather than applying a speculative double-encoding conversion. Existing fonts are read as stored; this does not repair already-corrupted names.

docs.title: Round 11 receipt corrections
docs.text:
Run upstream twice in separate fresh sessions: the command above records orphan fixtures; sh tests/native_drivers/run-round10.sh --suite upstream --native-attached records owned attached fixtures. The ledger keeps both native columns pending until C4 runs them. Each run resets fixture attribution per test, caches the ID map once and warms fontParts.test in a separate call. Parent assertion failures in attached mode stay unclassified; bare NotImplementedError is never a capability.

The glyph suite scans one glyph per call for hints. Choose a hinted GetGo fixture with --fixture; missing hints are an explicit failed prerequisite, not proof. The hinted write must refuse exactly glyph.geometry with unchanged payload/history. Supported glyph/flatten operations record one_history_row against historyStates. Bounds comparison keeps the native y convention and tolerates only 1e-6-unit numeric extrema drift (relative tolerance 1e-9), retaining both raw bounds. Undo/Redo activates the owned font first (mcptools.cpp:309–314 set_active_font). Save refusal skips close/reopen; reopen failure aborts dependent suite work. Retained raw native fixture references are released before final document close.

The deploy launcher is a startup script; never push its cold imports through run_python. Restart FontLab before suites to avoid already-loaded third-party package versions; warm-phase receipts include module origins.

docs.title: C4 re-run after Fontport T1–T13 repairs
docs.text:
The input is C4's FontLab 9.0.9783 evidence at workspace verification/issue-106/evidence/issue-105/round10/TICKETS.md. Original receipts remain untouched. These repairs are host-free and need fresh native proof.

Each command is a separate restarted, no-user-document session. The wrapper finds the workspace, supplies client dependencies and creates unique owned-copy outputs. No corpus or user font is written; owned documents close with close_font(save=False) in finally. Each native phase has a 3-second Python budget and a 4-second wall-time failure boundary, with polls between phases.

sh tests/native_drivers/run-round10.sh --suite glyph

docs.title: T9 source evidence
docs.text:
Read-only C++ root: <FontLab C++ source checkout> (FontLab Ltd. internal, read-only).

  • Font Info load/store uses weight_value/width_value and panose_string: Proteus/workspace2/fontinfo_data.cpp:391–402,586–596.
  • Their Python properties are bound at Proteus/pygate/pyflpackage.cpp:949,951, 1512–1516. Echopy fontlab.pyi declares weight_value, width_value and panose.
  • Master storage setters: Proteus/common/model/flpackage.cpp:17211–17220, 17350–17360. Master VFJ/history serialization writes the actual weight/width fields at :5853–5854 and Panose at :5875; reads at :4855–4860,4921–4925.
  • The old info setters write regenerated fg::Style data at Proteus/pygate/pyflpackage.cpp:2031–2078,2263–2287,2724–2758.
  • Real localized names are stored by Font Info via setLocalizedNames at fontinfo_data.cpp:520 and flpackage.cpp:16806–16836. That API has no Python binding in pyflpackage.cpp or echopy stubs. MCP's supported global write fields (Proteus/common/mcp/mcptools_fonts.cpp:469–565) omit localized/name records. Fontport therefore refuses changing name-record batches, including mixed batches, before history/data changes. It does not claim native support from the existence of the derived fg::Style setter.

T1 resolves actual native references rather than creating placeholders: MCP's class creation requires glyphListFromNames before commAddKerningGroup (Proteus/common/mcp/mcptools_metrics_kerning.cpp:709–715).

391 real upstream contour/segment/bPoint/point IDs also run host-free over a UFO backend that validates every forwarded contour using the actual FontGate point-pen adapter. This is geometry-contract coverage, not native Undo proof.
